Q: What explains the strange behavior of arguments in CMake macros (as opposed to functions)? A:

In short, inside a macro only literal ${..} constructions may refer to the macro's arguments. When used without surrounding ${} or when used with nested dereference, those constructions have no special meaning.

Details

You may treat calling the macro as plain inserting the macro's body into the caller point with literal replacement of expressions:

  • ${<param-name>} (where param-name is a name of the macro's parameter) with the value of the named macro's argument.
  • ${ARGV<n>} (where <n> is a literal number) with the value of the macro's positional argument.
  • ${ARGC} with the number of arguments actually passed to the macro
  • ${ARGV} with the list of all arguments passed to the macro
  • ${ARGN} with the list of arguments passed to the macro after the last named argument.

And only then the modified macro's body will be executed at the calling point.

E.g. if you write

macro (greetings name)
  message(STATUS "Hello, ${name}!")
  if (${ARGC} GREATER 1)
    message(STATUS "Hi, ${name}!")
  endif()
endmacro

message(STATUS "Call the macro")
greetings(human alien) # macro call

then when executing the macro call at the last line, CMake will expand it to

  message(STATUS "Hello, human!")
  if (2 GREATER 1)
    message(STATUS "Hi, alien!")
  endif()

which, upon execution, will print two line Hello, user! and Hi, alien!.

Note, that the macro's body modification is performed before execution of the first line from that body.

Now, if you write

macro(my_macro p)
    message("--my_macro--")
    message("p is: ${p}")
    if(p) # <========================= (1)
        message("\"if(p)\" evaluates to true")
    endif()
    set(i 1)
    message("ARGV${i}:${ARGV${i}}") <= (2)
endmacro()

my_macro(ON x)

then when executing the macro call at the last line, CMake will expand it to

    message("--my_macro--")
    message("p is: ON") # <= The only replacement!
    if(p) # <========================= (1)
        message("\"if(p)\" evaluates to true")
    endif()
    set(i 1)
    message("ARGV${i}:${ARGV${i}}") <= (2)

When execute the resulting code lines, variables p (in (1)) and ARGV1 (after the nested dereference in (2)) won't have any connection to the macro's context and will be treated as undefined.

Q: Regarding the issue that variables cannot be obtained using @forward in CSS preprocessor Sass A:

You can import as follows:

@use '@/assets/style/variables.scss' as * with ($theme: light);

@forward isn't needed unless you want other files to import variables through sidebar.scss

Q: Find the last (rightmost) non-null value on each row A:

It looks like "closest" means to favor the higher numbered columns ie 4,3,2,1. You can do that with just a coalesce

df.with_columns(
    desired_column=pl.coalesce(
        'col4', 'col3', 'col2', 'col1'
    )
)
shape: (9, 6)
┌────────────┬──────┬──────┬──────┬──────┬────────────────┐
│ product_id ┆ col1 ┆ col2 ┆ col3 ┆ col4 ┆ desired_column │
│ ---        ┆ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ ---  ┆ ---            │
│ str        ┆ str  ┆ str  ┆ str  ┆ str  ┆ str            │
╞════════════╪══════╪══════╪══════╪══════╪════════════════╡
│ 1          ┆ a    ┆ b    ┆ c    ┆ null ┆ c              │
│ 2          ┆ a    ┆ null ┆ null ┆ null ┆ a              │
│ 3          ┆ a    ┆ b    ┆ c    ┆ null ┆ c              │
│ 4          ┆ a    ┆ null ┆ null ┆ null ┆ a              │
│ 5          ┆ a    ┆ b    ┆ null ┆ null ┆ b              │
│ 6          ┆ a    ┆ null ┆ null ┆ d    ┆ d              │
│ 7          ┆ a    ┆ b    ┆ null ┆ null ┆ b              │
│ 8          ┆ a    ┆ null ┆ null ┆ null ┆ a              │
│ 9          ┆ a    ┆ b    ┆ null ┆ d    ┆ d              │
└────────────┴──────┴──────┴──────┴──────┴────────────────┘

You can do it more dynamically with a generator:

pl.coalesce(x for x in df.columns[::-1] if x!='product_id')

Q: FCM Notifications fail to arrive (on device) when internet is slightly disturbed - Flutter A:

Hey 👋 — this is a very real issue, and you’re not imagining things.
Short version: this behavior is expected (and mostly by design), and WhatsApp is the exception, not the rule.

I’ll break it down clearly and then give you what you should and should not do on both iOS and Android.

What’s actually happening?

FCM (and APNs underneath it) maintains a long-lived TCP connection to the push service.

When you do this:

  • Wi-Fi hotspot stays connected ✅
  • Backhaul (mobile data) drops for 1–2 seconds ❌
  • Network interface does not fully disconnect

You end up with:

A half-open / stale socket
The OS thinks the network is still valid
FCM thinks it’s still connected
But packets are silently dropped

This is a classic mobile networking edge case.

Why notifications stop

  • No clean disconnect event
  • No TCP reset
  • No OS-level “network changed” signal
  • So FCM never retries aggressively

This is why:

  • Microsoft Teams ❌ breaks
  • Slack ❌ breaks
  • Gmail ❌ sometimes breaks
  • WhatsApp ✅ works

Why WhatsApp works (important insight)

WhatsApp does NOT rely solely on FCM/APNs.

They have:

  • Persistent app-level sockets
  • Aggressive heartbeat + reconnect logic
  • Their own fallback polling system
  • Server-side delivery confirmation

You and I cannot do this without system-level privileges.

So don’t benchmark against WhatsApp — benchmark against Teams, Slack, Gmail.
Your results already prove this is OS-level behavior.

iOS: Is your workaround valid?

What you’re doing

// Unregister from APNs
UIApplication.shared.unregisterForRemoteNotifications()

// Re-register
UIApplication.shared.registerForRemoteNotifications()

Does it work?

✅ Yes

Is it safe?

⚠️ Technically allowed, but not recommended as a primary fix

Apple’s stance (implicitly):

  • APNs connection lifecycle is OS-managed
  • Apps should not force reconnections
  • Excessive re-registration can:
    • Trigger throttling
    • Cause token churn
    • Increase battery usage

When it’s acceptable

✔ Triggered rarely
✔ After a confirmed network change
✔ As a last-resort recovery, not a loop

What NOT to do

❌ On every connectivity blip
❌ On every app resume
❌ On a timer

If you keep it:

  • Guard it carefully
  • Rate-limit it
  • Log when it happens

iOS: What you SHOULD do instead

1. Detect real network transitions

Use NWPathMonitor (native) or a Flutter plugin that wraps it properly.

Trigger recovery only when:

  • Path changes
  • Interface changes (Wi-Fi ↔ cellular)
  • Connection was previously lost

2. Let FCM refresh tokens naturally

FirebaseMessaging.instance.onTokenRefresh.listen((token) {
    // Send token to backend
});

3. Accept that APNs is eventually consistent

Apple will eventually fix the socket.
There is no guaranteed immediate recovery API.

Android: Why there’s no fix (and why that code is misleading)

The diagnostic code:

*#*#426#*#*

Shows:

FCM service connection, not real internet reachability

So this situation:

  • FCM shows “Connected”
  • Backhaul is dead
  • No packets flow

Is completely possible.

Why Android behaves this way

  • Same long-lived socket model
  • Same half-open TCP problem
  • Same OS ownership

What you can (and can’t) do on Android

❌ You cannot

  • Force FCM reconnect
  • Restart Google Play Services
  • Reset the socket manually

✅ You can

  • Detect connectivity changes
  • Wake the app
  • Let FCM naturally re-establish

Best practice on Android

FirebaseMessaging.onMessageOpenedApp.listen(...)
FirebaseMessaging.onMessage.listen(...)

And design your backend assuming missed pushes.

The uncomfortable truth (but important)

Push notifications are not guaranteed delivery systems

They are:

  • Best-effort
  • Eventually consistent
  • OS-controlled
  • Optimized for battery, not reliability

Every serious app does this

  • Push = wake-up hint
  • App fetches actual state from backend
  • Missed push ≠ missed data

Final recommendations (TL;DR)

✅ Do this

  • Treat push as advisory, not authoritative
  • Sync state when app resumes
  • Handle missed notifications gracefully
  • Log and monitor token refreshes
  • Use your iOS workaround sparingly

❌ Don’t do this

  • Force re-registration aggressively
  • Expect FCM to reconnect instantly
  • Benchmark against WhatsApp

Your understanding is correct

“As soon as the internet slightly disturbed, the FCM does not reconnect and the connection goes stale.”

✔ Correct
✔ Observed by many production apps
✔ OS-level behavior
✔ Not a Flutter bug
✔ Not your implementation mistake

Q: Codeigniter query error: "In aggregated query without GROUP BY, expression #1 of SELECT list contains nonaggregated column" A:

you are facing this problem because of the ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY option in the MYSQL so kindly set,

SET GLOBAL sql_mode=(SELECT REPLACE(@@sql_mode,'ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY',''));

to solve the issue.
